parser_finding.severity: non-blocking, silent field loss (not a crash)
parser_finding.description: The live page's DOM has drifted from the assumption baked into _parse_member_info (and the SAMPLE_HTML test fixture): peer_type ('Life peer' / 'Excepted Hereditary' / etc.) is no longer a second 'secondary-info' div next to party. It is now rendered as '.indicator.indicator-label' inside '.info .info-inner .indicators-left', a sibling block outside 'content'. _parse_member_info only reads card.find_all(class_='secondary-info')[1], which no longer exists, so peer_type resolves to '' for all 789/789 captured members. Confirmed by direct count: 0 of 789 cards have a second secondary-info div; all 789 have an indicator-label element carrying the real peer type. member_id, name, party, category, interest description text, ceased-date parsing, and counterparty extraction are all unaffected and verified correct against this capture.
parser_finding.impact: Entity.properties['peer_type'] is stored as an empty string instead of the real value for every Lords Entity created from a live (non-archival) capture. Does not affect edge/attestation creation, company matching, or the retrieval controls above (none of which depend on peer_type).
parser_finding.recommendation: Not fixed here per task scope (capture + control set only, no parser edits). If peer_type is needed downstream, _parse_member_info needs an additional selector for '.indicator-label' as a fallback/replacement for the second secondary-info div.

scope_limits.closes: The Lords-stratum RETRIEVAL control gap: the pipeline can now be tested against a frozen, hashed, byte-verified snapshot of the live Lords register — 789/789 members and 5174/5174 interest entries parse without failure, and the 12 controls above are independently checkable register-visible ground truth (peer, member ID, declared company, exact wording, page).
scope_limits.does_not_close: The Lords-stratum TEMPORAL gap. The Lords register publishes NO per-entry registration/start dates (Edge.valid_from is always null by design — see lords_interests.py module docstring). The earliest Wayback Machine capture of this page is 2020-06-17, which postdates most of the 24 award cases in scope, so level-2 'pre-award observed' evidence remains unavailable for 20 of 24 cases.
scope_limits.conclusion: Lords supports the ATEMPORAL secondary endpoint with validated retrieval (this control set). The strict temporal endpoint stays instrument-limited for the Lords stratum — this capture does not change that.
